title: Scaling Laws of SignSGD in Linear Regression: When Does It Outperform SGD?
abstract:
We study scaling laws of signSGD under a power-law random features (PLRF) model that accounts for both feature and target decay.
We analyze the population risk of a linear model trained with one-pass signSGD on Gaussian-sketched features. 
We express the risk as a function of model size, training steps, learning rate, and the feature and target decay parameters.
Comparing against the SGD risk analyzed by Paquette et al. (2024), we identify a drift-normalization effect and a noise-reshaping effect unique to signSGD.
We then obtain compute-optimal scaling laws under the optimal choice of learning rate. Our analysis shows that the noise-reshaping effect can make the compute-optimal slope of signSGD steeper than that of SGD in regimes where noise is dominant.
Finally, we observe that the widely used warmup-stable-decay (WSD) schedule further reduces the noise term and sharpens the compute-optimal slope, when feature decay is fast but target decay is slow.
problem: Scaling laws and compute-optimal performance of signSGD under realistic data distributions with power-law feature and target decay are not well understood.
approach: Analysis of signSGD under power-law random features model characterizes population risk as a function of model size, training steps, and learning rate, identifying drift-normalization and noise-reshaping effects unique to signSGD.
contribution: signSGD can achieve steeper compute-optimal slopes than SGD in noise-dominant regimes, and the warmup-stable-decay schedule further reduces noise and sharpens the optimal slope.
